stimulus:
"Hope" is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -

And sweetest - in the Gale - is heard -
And sore must be the storm -
That could abash the little Bird
That kept so many warm -

I've heard it in the chillest land -
And on the strangest Sea -
Yet - never - in Extremity,
It asked a crumb - of me.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing before and after drug (the 'feathered' pre-existing bird)
ideas.description: Label a clonal population with heritable expressed DNA barcodes, split it into replicates, and treat them with the drug. Sequence the surviving barcodes to test whether the same sister lineages survive across replicates (pre-existing, heritable state) or different ones each time (stochastic induction). Pair this with single-cell RNA-seq of sibling cells sampled before treatment, so that pre-treatment transcriptional states can be linked to each lineage's later fate.

ideas.title: Live-cell single-cell tracking with reporters of signaling and stress states
ideas.description: Use time-lapse microscopy with fluorescent reporters (e.g., ERK/AKT activity, apoptosis caspase sensor, cell cycle FUCCI) to follow thousands of cells for days before, during, and after drug exposure. Retrospectively align the dynamics of cells that survive with those that die, to find early features such as pulsatile signaling, slow cycling, or mitochondrial priming that predict survival. The 'song without words' is the dynamic pattern rather than a static level.

ideas.title: Multi-omic profiling of persisters over time, including chromatin accessibility
ideas.description: Run joint scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CUT&Tag for histone marks) on untreated cells, cells at early drug exposure, persisters, and cells after drug withdrawal. This tests whether survival depends on reversible epigenetic states, such as an open-chromatin stress-response or drug-tolerant program, and whether those states can be inherited. Perturbing the identified regulators (e.g., KDM5, HDAC) would then test causality.

ideas.title: Mother-daughter inheritance and state-switching rate measurements
ideas.description: Sort cells by a candidate marker of tolerance (e.g., a high-expressing subpopulation) and measure how quickly the population returns to the original marker distribution, using fluctuation-analysis or Luria-Delbrück-style experiments and mathematical modeling. Fit models to estimate switching rates and memory duration, and use time-lapse of cell pairs to measure how similar sister cells are in fate. This quantifies whether tolerance is a fast-fluctuating state or a stable, heritable one.

ideas.title: Pooled CRISPR screens with drug plus metabolic and survival-pathway readouts in persisters
ideas.description: Perform genome-wide or focused CRISPRi/a screens under drug treatment, selecting for cells that survive the first days rather than for stable resistance. Combine this with measurements of persister metabolism (oxidative phosphorylation, lipid peroxidation or GPX4 dependence, ATP/ROS) and drug-efflux activity. This identifies the genes and vulnerabilities that make survival possible and tests whether blocking them eliminates the surviving fraction.
